In the past two weeks (48–49), syndromic surveillance in Yap State reported an increase in diarrheoa cases (10 and 13 cases, respectively) above their threshold of 6 cases. The majority of cases were reported from the main referral hospital. No testing has been conducted at the moment to confirm the aetiology. A grey alert is added

In Week 49, a total of 133 new cases were detected out of 359 tests conducted. The number of confirmed cases identified, and the positivity rate (37%) decreased, although this does not confirm a decline in the epidemic. Biological diagnosis is no longer carried out systematically, and the number of cases is probably underestimated. The number of new admissions remained stable overall in Week 49, with 12 people hospitalized, including 2 in ICU. No deaths have been reported. The red alert is maintained.

The number of ILI cases decreased from 40 cases in EW48 to 37 cases in EW49. Overall, ILI cases have decreased by 17% in EW49 compared to the previous three Epi Weeks. Out of the thirty-seven ILI cases, 24 are as follows: one COVID-19, two Flu A, one Flu A + RSV, one Flu A & B, one Flu B, one Pneumonia, one RSV, 7 Streptococcus, 9 Upper Respiratory Infection. Cases reported are still above the three-year average, and as a result, the blue alert is maintained.

On December 9, four individuals with Dengue-like symptoms were observed at the hospital, followed by six more people with similar symptoms the next day. In total, 21 individuals displaying Dengue-like symptoms were seen at the hospital between 9 to 14 December. Two suspected cases were tested using a rapid test, both yielding positive results for Dengue. Due to a lack of available rapid tests to assess all suspected cases, the situation is being treated as Dengue on Atafu, with a total of 57 suspected cases reported until 5 pm December 14. As a result, a red alert is added.

The Ministry of Health and Medical Services in Fiji has confirmed a typhoid outbreak in Lau Settlement in Ra, with six cases reported from September to December, resulting in one death. Response measures include contact tracing, community awareness, house-to-house inspections, direct supervision of mass gatherings, and water sampling. Planned measures involve providing field latrines, mass screening, and administering the typhoid conjugate vaccine to prevent further spread, while the public is advised against non-essential travel to the affected area and urged to prioritize good hygiene practices during the festive season. As a result, the blue alert is changed to red alert and the star is removed.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: In week 01, a total of 4 diarrhoeal cases have been reported. Cases have been below threshold for the past two weeks and as a result, the red alert is changed to blue alert. – Source: Yap State Department of Health Services Communicable Disease report week 1 published on 10 January 2024.

As of 18 December 2023, a total of 57 suspected cases reported until 5 pm on the day of the report. All cases have no travel history. As the latest update received was dated more than 4 weeks, a star is added. – Source: Tokelau Dengue Outbreak in Atafu situation report published on 18 December 2023.

During week S02, 15 new cases of influenza were confirmed out of 78 test results, with 13 cases identified as influenza A. There were five hospital admissions reported, but none in intensive care, and the positivity rate was lower than the previous week. The ongoing epidemic also involves the circulation of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza virus, emphasizing the importance of seasonal vaccination campaigns and adherence to barrier measures to limit the impact of respiratory infection epidemics. The red alert is maintained. - Source : Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°02-2024 posted on PacNet on 19 January

In week 3, a total of 13 diarrhoea cases have been reported. Cases reported are above the threshold of 6 cases.  No testing was conducted for this reported period. The blue alert is maintained. Source: –Yap State Department of Health Services, Communicable Disease Report, Week 3 - Facebook accessed on 30 January 2024

On December 22, 2023, an outbreak was declared in the Lau settlement in Ra, with 6 cases, including one fatality, reported for the period from September to December 2023. Public Health response measures have been initiated to address the situation, including contact tracing, community awareness campaigns, house-to-house inspections, mass screening and administration of the Typhoid vaccine. It has been 35 days since the last update, and as a result, a star is added to the alert map.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: During the period from 01/01 to 26/01, a total of two cases were detected. Since that start of the outbreak in December 2023, 5 cases have been hospitalized, due to loss of appetite and dehydration. All cases were mild, and no deaths were reported.  The star is removed, and the alert is changed to blue. – Source: Personal communication with country focal point on 26 January 2024.

In week 4, two new confirmed cases were detected out of the 94 samples tested, and two additional cases were detected in week 05. These brings the number of confirmed indigenous cases to 10 since 27 November 2023. These cases were from Papeete, Mahina, Faaa, Punaauia and Moorea. Of these cases, 3 people have been hospitalised. In Punaauia, the 2 cases are epidemiologically linked and constitute the first cluster identified. In Tahiti and Moorea, this situation corresponds to the level 2 alert phase of the dengue. A red alert is added.  Source : Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°04-2024 posted on PacNet on 03 February 2024

In week 04, 13 new Influenza A cases were confirmed from 106 samples tested. From the cases reported, four were hospitalised with no admissions to intensive care. Additionally, Mycoplasma pneumoniae and RSV were identified. The red alert is maintained. - Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°04-2024 posted on PacNet on 03 February 2024

As of January 30, 2024, the epidemic threshold has been exceeded since EW01 of 2024. There have been a total of 13 hospital admissions, including 3 in intensive care, leading to the death of a 36-year-old man in week 4, 2024. A total of 191 cases have been confirmed in Wallis and Futuna since 29 August 2023, including 164 in Wallis and 27 in Futuna. Virus typing was requested, results are still pending. A red alert has been added. Source: Rapport de situation circulation du sar-cov2 a Wallis et Futuna au 30/01/2024 shared on email on 30 January 2024.

As of 23 January, the Tokelau Health Department has recorded 130 dengue fever cases since an outbreak began on 09 December 2023. All cases were mild, five people were admitted to hospital for loss of appetite and dehydration and no deaths were reported Testing to confirm dengue serotype is underway. The last update was provided 2 weeks ago and as a result, a star is added to the alert map. Source: Personal communication with country official on 31 January 2024.

From 28 August 2023 to 19 February 2024, a total of 210 confirmed COVID-19 cases were detected. This includes 13 individuals requiring hospitalization, including three in intensive care, leading to one death in week 04, 2024. There has been a decrease in the number of cases detected since 8 February, and as a result, the alert is changed to blue.

In week 08, there were no new confirmed dengue cases among the 75 samples tested. However, six additional cases have been identified in week 09, which brings the total number of cases to 22 since beginning of 2024. All reported cases were locally acquired, and there have been no new hospitalizations. Among the 22 cases, 12 were in Tahiti, 6 in Moorea, and 4 in Rangiroa

During week 08, eight new cases of influenza were confirmed out of 85 tests conducted, all identified as Influenza A. Two cases required hospitalization, but none were admitted to the intensive care unit. The hospitalization rate increased compared to the previous week, indicating the continuing flu epidemic. Additionally, RSV has been detected. Since Influenza B was last detected in week 02, the Influenza A & B alert has been changed to Influenza A and the blue alert is maintained

From January 29th to February 28th, a total of 1,039 diarrhoeal cases were reported. Laboratory testing has been conducted, confirming 46 cases with rotavirus infection, of which 89% of the cases were children under five years old. Thirty of these cases required hospitalization and no deaths have been reported so far. Public health interventions including health promotional messages, vaccination for children and surveillance activities have been implemented to address the outbreak situation.

From August 28, 2023, to February 19, 2024, a total of 210 confirmed COVID-19 cases were identified. Among these cases, 13 individuals required hospitalization, including three in intensive care, resulting in one death in week 04, 2024. The most recent update was provided more than two weeks ago and as a result, a star is added to blue alert on the map. Source : Bulletin de surveillance épidémiologique 01/2024 – Semaines 31/2023 a 7/2024 Données du 01/08/2023 au 19/02/2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 23 February 2024.

In EpiWeek 10, five new dengue cases were reported out of 62 samples tested. Furthermore, three additional cases were detected in EpiWeek 11, bringing the total to 32 cases since the beginning of 2024. Serotyping tests have confirmed Dengue Serotype 2 (DENV-2). A 57-year-old individual was hospitalised in week 10, the fifth dengue-related hospitalisation reported since the start of the year. The majority of the confirmed cases are from Tahiti.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In week 10, seven new influenza A cases were confirmed out of 67 tests conducted. Five of these cases were hospitalised. The flu epidemic is ongoing. Additionally, RSV has been identified and is circulating.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: From 29 January to 14 March, there were a total of 3,268 cases of diarrhoea reported from Tarawa and Betio Atoll. Among these cases, 69 tested positive for rotavirus, with 87% affecting children under the age of five. Of the rotavirus-positive cases, 37 required hospitalisation. There were six reported deaths, all of which were children under the age of five. Additionally, Giardia and amoeba were identified.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In EpiWeek 9, two new dengue cases were reported in Samoa, bringing the number of confirmed cases to 24 since the beginning of February 2024. Samples have been sent for serotype testing in New Zealand, and results are pending.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In French Polynesia, reported cases of dengue fever decreased from five in EpiWeek 10 to two in EpiWeek 11, bringing the total number to 32 confirmed and two probable cases since November 2023. There were no hospitalisations reported during this period. The majority of cases were reported from Tahiti. The alert is changed to blue.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In epiWeek 11, three new cases of Influenza A were confirmed out of 97 samples tested. Two of these cases required hospitalization, with none in the ICU. The positivity rate is decreasing from the previous week, indicating that the seasonal epidemic of influenza appears to be coming to an end. The blue alert is maintained.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Between January 29 and March 22, 2024, a total of 4,088 cases of diarrheoa were reported, with laboratory testing confirming 69 cases of Rotavirus, primarily affecting children under 5 years old (60 cases). Out of these, 37 cases required hospitalisation, and six deaths were reported, all among children under 5 years, occurring within a downward trend in the number of suspected cases since 12 March 2024. The red alert is maintained.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In EpiWeek 10, Samoa reported 12 new cases of dengue, totalling 38 cases since February 2024. The most affected age groups are individuals between 20 – 29 years old and those over 60 years. The affected areas are primarily located in the Northwest of Upolu (NWU) and the Apia Urban Area regions. Serotyping results are pending. The red alert is maintained.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Between 23-29 March, 525 new diarrheoa cases were reported, bringing the total cases to 4,613 since 29 January 2024. Laboratory testing has confirmed 14 additional cases of Rotavirus, bringing the total number to 83 cases, of which 76 are children under 5 years old. Two new deaths were reported, bringing the total to 8 deaths since beginning of March, all among children under 5 years old, occurring within a downward trend in the number of suspected cases since March 12, 2024. The red alert is changed to blue.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In EpiWeek 14, zero cases reported from 60 samples tested. In EpiWeek 15, one additional case was identified on 8th of April bringing the total number of cases to 42 (37 confirmed and 5 probable). Majority of the cases are from Tahiti. There were no new hospitalisations reported during this reporting period. There is co-circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2 serotypes, with a predominance of the DENV-2 serotype. The blue alert is maintained. - Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°14 -2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 13 April 2024.

In EpiWeek 14, eight new cases of Influenza (seven influenza A and one influenza B) were confirmed out of 74 tests conducted. Two hospitalisations reported with none in the ICU. The positivity rate was slightly up compared to the previous week, with the seasonal epidemic of influenza apparently ongoing, alongside the circulation of other respiratory viruses including RSV. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°14 -2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 05 April 2024.

In EpiWeek 13, 33 new laboratory-confirmed dengue cases were recorded, bringing the total to 73 cases in March so far, with case counts continuing to increase. Serotype results are still pending. The most affected age groups are those between 5-9 years old and over 60 years old. The red alert is maintained. - Source: Samoa Ministry of Health Dengue Situation Report #6, EpiWeek 13: 25 – 31 March 2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 15 April 2024.

In EpiWeek 15, one new case of dengue was reported among 74 samples tested. As of 18 April, EpiWeek 16, four additional cases were identified, bringing the total to 46 cases (41 confirmed, 5 probables). Of these, 25 were from Tahiti, 10 from Moora, 7 from Rangiroa, with single cases from Bora Bora, Fakarava, and a visiting case with onset less than 15 days after arrival. There is co-circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2 serotypes, with a predominance of the DENV-2 serotype.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In EpiWeek 15, 20 new cases of Influenza A and one new case of Influenza B were confirmed out of 76 tests conducted. Seven cases were hospitalised, with one admitted to the ICU (Intensive Care Unit). Among the hospitalised cases, 3 were over 60 years old and 2 were between the ages of 55-59 years. An investigation is underway into potential comorbidities. The rate of positive tests has increased in the previous weeks, indicating a new epidemic wave of Influenza A. The blue alert has been changed to red alert for Influenza A
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: In EpiWeeks 14 & 15, 82 new laboratory-confirmed dengue cases were reported, bringing the total to 216 cases since November 2023 to April 14, 2024. On April 19, 2024, a dengue fever outbreak was declared in Samoa by the Ministry of Health due to the surge in reported cases, with approximately 80 percent of cases concentrated on Upolu Island, particularly in the northwest. A national cleanup campaign and fumigation program have been launched to target mosquito breeding sites, focusing on vulnerable groups like children aged 5-9 years, seniors aged 65+ years, and individuals with health complications, while awaiting serotype results.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: On April 29, 2024, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services declared dengue fever outbreaks in Ovalau (Eastern Division) and the Western Division, where case numbers exceed expected levels for this time of year with serotype results pending. In Ovalau, 72 cases have been reported since January 1st, with a recent surge observed in the past two weeks, predominantly affecting the 10-19 age group. In the Western Division, 370 cases have been reported since the beginning of the year, with recent surges noted in Nadi, Ba, and Tavua. The Ministry emphasises ongoing public awareness campaigns, community engagement, and early medical consultation for suspected cases to address the outbreak.  A red alert is added to the map.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: On April 29, 2024, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services declared  leptospirosis outbreaks in Kadavu (Eastern Division) and the Western Division due to significantly elevated case numbers beyond expected levels, particularly in recent weeks. In Kadavu, 31 laboratory-confirmed cases have been reported since the beginning of the year, predominantly affecting the 10-19 year age group. In the Western Division, 212 cases have been reported since the start of the year, with a surge observed in the Lautoka and Ba medical subdivisions, prompting heightened surveillance, clinical management training, and collaboration with animal health authorities to mitigate transmission risks.  A red alert is added to the map.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: From 25 April to 01 May, three new cases of leptospirosis have been reported in Ambae island, Penama province. This brings the total to 10 cases since 15th of April 2024, with no deaths reported. The Ministry of Health had deployed a national surge team to assist with the response in Ambae. The red alert is maintained.

In EpiWeek 18, one dengue case was confirmed out of 55 samples tested (this case was reported as detected last week). No new cases were detected in EpiWeek 19. source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

Two cases from EpiWeek 25 were hospitalised but have recovered, with DENV-1 identified as the serotype. The latest DENV-1 case dates from EpiWeek 13. In EpiWeek 32, five new dengue cases were confirmed out of 27 samples tested, including 3 residents in Tahiti, 1 resident in Nuku-Hiva and one tourist who travelled to Fakarava (Tuamotu Archipelago) and Tahiti during the contagious period. From 06 to 12 August, 573 additional COVID-19 cases have been reported. The data indicates a decrease from 11.7% to 11% average test positivity rate and 88 average daily COVID-19 cases statewide over the 7-day period. An daily average of 72 hospitalisations were reported between 8 to 14 August. Additionally, there were six patients in ICU.  A retrospectove review of deaths occurring from late June through July resulted in 22 additional COVID-19 related deaths added. The Department of Health Respiratory Disease Dashboard shows that COVID-19 activity is at a medium level with a decreasing trend. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Disease Outbreak Control Division | COVID-19 | State of Hawai'i - Department of Health (hawaii.gov) accessed on 20 August 2024

In EpiWeek 32, CNMI reported a decrease in COVID-19 cases from 31 in EpiWeek 31 to 19 in EpiWeek 32, marking a 57% decrease compared to the previous three weeks. There were two COVID-19 hospitalisations recorded in EpiWeek 32. The blue alert is maintained.  – Source: CNMI Weekly Surveillance Report 2024 – EPI Week 32 shared to PPHSN focal point on 15 August 2024.

Between July 31 and August 14, 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department reported four new typhoid cases. Since June 5, 86 cases have been diagnosed, with 20 requiring hospitalisation. The laboratory confirmed 21 tests positive for typhoid fever were referred from Tungaru Central Hospital laboratory and confirmed at the Microbiological Diagnostic Unit – Public Health Laboratory, Doherty Institute in Melbourne, Australia. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (5) shared with PPHSN focal point on 26 August 2024.

In EpiWeek 34, eight new dengue cases were confirmed out of 45 samples tested, including 6 residents in Tahiti, 1 resident in Nuku-Hiva and 1 tourist. The total number of reported cases is 130 (119 confirmed cases and 11 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases, no case was hospitalised in Week 34. DENV-2 has been identified in 61% of the cases. The alert phase is maintained, with active dengue circulation in Tahiti and Nuku-Hiva. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°34 -2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 03 September 2024

Between July 14 and August 29, 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department reported 16 new typhoid cases. Since June 5, a total of 102 cases have been diagnosed, with 20 requiring hospitalisation. The laboratory confirmed 21 tests positive for typhoid fever, which were referred from the Tungaru Central Hospital laboratory and confirmed at the Microbiological Diagnostic Unit – Public Health Laboratory, Doherty Institute in Melbourne, Australia. No confirmed positive cases have been reported since Thursday, September 5. The Ministry of Health & Medical Services continues its community awareness efforts. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (6) shared with PPHSN focal point on 06 September 2024.

In EpiWeek 37, five new dengue cases were confirmed out of 36 samples tested, including 3 residents in Tahiti, 1 resident in Fakarava (Tuamotu Archipelago) and 1 tourist. The total number of reported cases is 146 (133 confirmed cases and 13 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases, no case was hospitalised in Week 37. The positivity rate remains stable at around 15%. The alert phase is maintained, with active dengue circulation in Tahiti, Moorea and Nuku-Hiva. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°37 - 2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 24 September 2024.

Between 14 June and 19 September, 115 confirmed cases of pertussis were reported. In EpiWeek 37, 16 new cases were notified, all residents in Tahiti. As of 19 September five new cases were recorded beginning of EpiWeek 37. Out of the cases investigated, seven children required hospitalisation, including five infants aged 3 months or younger. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°37 - 2024 shared with PPHSN focal point on 24 September 2024.

As of 20 September, 47 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024. Since the beginning of September, 26 cases have been notified, with the most recent case dated 18 September 2024. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie (gouv.nc) accessed on 24 September 2024.

Between August 29 and September 23, 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department reported 4 new typhoid cases. Since June 5, a total of 106 cases have been diagnosed, with 20 requiring hospitalisations. The laboratory confirmed 22 tests positive for typhoid fever, which were referred from the Tungaru Central Hospital laboratory and confirmed at the Microbiological Diagnostic Unit – Public Health Laboratory, Doherty Institute in Melbourne, Australia. Because of the decreasing number of notified cases the red alert is changed to a blue alert. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (7) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 24 September 2024.

In EpiWeek 39, 11 new dengue cases were confirmed out of 37 samples tested, including seven residents in Tahiti, one resident in Huahine (Society Islands archipelago), one resident in Fakarava (Tuamotu Archipelago) and two tourists with one of the tourists visiting Huahine during the contagious phase. The total number of reported cases is 165 (152 confirmed cases and 13 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases, no new hospitalisations, severe cases, or deaths were reported in Week 39. The overall positivity rate increased to 30% in week 39, reflecting an upward trend observed over the past four weeks. Since November 27, 2023, among 127 serotyped samples, DENV-2 was identified in 52% of cases and DENV-1 in 48%. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°39 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 October 2024.

Between 14 June and 29 September, 131 confirmed cases of pertussis were reported. In EpiWeek 39, eight new cases were notified, including six residents in Tahiti, one resident in Moorea and one resident in Rangiroa (Tuamotu Archipelago). The majority of reported cases are individuals aged 7 to 79 years (61%), and 14% are infants (<1 year old). The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°39 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 October 2024.

As of 7 October, 63 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024 out of 479 samples tested. In September, 36 cases have been notified. Since the 1st of October, six cases were reported, with the most recent case dated 06 October 2024. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie (gouv.nc) accessed on 08 October 2024.

In EpiWeek 40, nine new dengue cases were confirmed from 49 samples tested, including seven residents of Tahiti. Two clusters have been identified—one in Paofai and the other in Miri. The total number of reported cases is 174 (161 confirmed cases and 13 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases, one new hospitalisation was reported in a 10-year-old patient (with a length of stay of 1 day). No severe cases or deaths were reported in Week 40. The overall positivity rate decreased to 18% in Week 40. Additionally, in EpiWeek 41, two new dengue cases were reported in Ua Pou (Marquesas Islands), marking the first case on this island. Since November 27, 2023, among 132 serotyped samples, DENV-2 was identified in 50% of cases and DENV-1 in 50%. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°40 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 15 October 2024.

Between 14 June and 06 October, 146 confirmed pertussis cases were reported. In EpiWeek 40, 15 new cases were notified, including 13 residents of Tahiti and two residents of Rangiroa (Tuamotu Archipelago). One of the cases in Rangiroa has an epidemiological link to a previous case, suggesting circulation on the island. The majority of reported cases are individuals aged 7 to 79 years (83%), while 17% are infants (<1 year old). Among all investigated cases, 10 children required hospitalisation, including 8 infants aged 8 months or younger. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°40 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 15 October 2024.

Between August 29 and October 08, 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department, reported two new typhoid cases. Since June 5, a total of 108 cases have been diagnosed, with 21 requiring hospitalisation. The laboratory confirmed 22 tests positive for typhoid fever, which were referred from the Tungaru Central Hospital laboratory and confirmed at the Microbiological Diagnostic Unit – Public Health Laboratory, Doherty Institute in Melbourne, Australia. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (8) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 October 2024.

As of 13 October 2024, 62 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024, out of 514 samples tested. In September, 33 cases have been notified. Since the 1st of October, eight cases were reported, with the most recent case dated 11 October 2024. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie (gouv.nc) accessed on 15 October 2024.

From 8 to 22 October 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department, reported four new suspected typhoid cases and one new confirmed positive case. Since June 5, a total of 112 cases (23 laboratory confirmed and 89 suspected cases) have been diagnosed, with 21 requiring hospitalisation. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (9) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 22 October 2024.

In EpiWeek 42, 18 new dengue cases were confirmed from 73 samples tested, including twelve residents of Tahiti, two residents of Moorea, one resident from Huahine and one resident from Bora-Bora (both in Society Islands archipelago). The total number of reported cases is 207 (191 confirmed cases and 16 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases there were two hospitalisations in short stay unit reported in Week 42, for a 9-year-old child and an 18-year-old. No severe cases or deaths were reported since November 2023. The positivity rate is stable (25% in EpiWeek 42). Additionally, in EpiWeek 43, two new dengue cases were confirmed in two visitors: one who visited Huahine and the other Raiatea (Society Islands archipelago). Since November 27, 2023, among 154 serotyped samples, DENV-2 was identified in 44% of cases and DENV-1 in 56%. Cases have occurred in isolation or small family or neighbourhood clusters, mainly affecting children and young adults, often recent residents of French Polynesia. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°42 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 29 October 2024.

Between 14 June and 20 October, 191 confirmed pertussis cases were reported. In EpiWeek 42, 33 new cases were notified, in residents of Tahiti and Moorea. In EpiWeek 43, as of the 22 October, 24 confirmed cases have already been reported. A cluster of at least nine cases (probable and confirmed) has been identified in a school in Papeete. Among all cases investigated, 10 children required hospitalisation, including 8 infants aged 8 months or younger. The positivity rate is stable (12% in EpiWeek 42). The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°42 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 29 October 2024.

As of 13 October 2024, and since the beginning of the year, 79 cases of pertussis have been reported, out of 497 samples tested. Among them 62 cases were attributed to Bordetella pertussis and 17 to Bordetella parapertussis. The majority of the cases are in females (67%), and children aged 0 to 14 years (44%), including four infants under six months. The Southern Province has the highest number of cases, representing 57% of the total, with an incidence rate of 2.2 per 10,000 inhabitants. The Islands Province accounts for 27% of cases, corresponding to an incidence rate of 11.4 per 10,000 inhabitants. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Point épidémiologique (Données arrêtées au 13 octobre 2024) – Epidémie de coqueluche shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 25 October 2024.

In EpiWeek 43, 16 new dengue cases were confirmed from 68 samples tested, including ten residents of Tahiti, one resident of Rangiroa (Tuamotu Archipelago), and four visitors. The total number of reported cases is 225 (208 confirmed cases and 17 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. Among the recent cases, one short-stay hospitalisation was reported, with no severe cases or deaths since November 2023. The positivity rate remains stable at 23.5% in EpiWeek 43. Additionally, in EpiWeek 44, seven new dengue cases were confirmed, including residents of Tahiti, Moorea, Huahine, and one visitor. Since November 27, 2023, among 171 serotyped samples, DENV-2 was identified in 40% of cases and DENV-1 in 60%. Since late July, DENV-1 has become the predominant serotype in the country. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°43 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 05 November 2024.

Between 14 June and 27 October, 254 confirmed pertussis cases were reported. In EpiWeek 43, 62 new cases were notified, including residents of Tahiti and Taha’a (part of the Society Islands) marking the first case on this island. No hospitalisation was reported in EpiWeek 43. In EpiWeek 44, the first case of pertussis was reported in a resident of Fakahina (Tuamotu Archipelago), who had stayed in Tahiti and Bora-Bora during their exposure period. Most cases (83%) are individuals aged 7 to 79, the proportion of school-aged children affected has nearly tripled since week 41, indicating active spread of pertussis in schools. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°43 - 2024 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 05 November 2024

From 8 to 22 October 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department, reported four new suspected typhoid cases and one new confirmed positive case. Since 5 June, a total of 112 cases (23 laboratory confirmed and 89 suspected cases) have been diagnosed, with 21 requiring hospitalisations. It has been 3 weeks since the last update, and as a result, a star is added to the blue alert. – Source: Typhoid Outbreak Situation Report (9) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 22 October 2024.

As of 07 November 2024, 74 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024, out of 630 samples tested. In October, 22 cases have been notified compared to 31 notified cases in September. Since the 1st of November, one case was reported, with the most recent case dated 02 November 2024. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie accessed on 12 November 2024.

From 28 October to 3 November, 2024, 236 watery diarrheoa cases were reported in Vanuatu. The number of cases continues to exceed the alert threshold (158 cases per week). Efate Island recorded 222 of these cases. This is the first watery diarrheoa outbreak in 2024, primarily affecting the younger population (73% of cases are in children aged 5 years and under). During the reporting period, 3 cases were admitted to the hospital, and no deaths have been reported. Consequently, the grey alert for diarrhea is maintained, pending confirmation of the causative agent. – Source: Watery Diarrhoea in Efate Situation Update 02 (Report Date: 08 November 2024/ Covering Period from 01 January – 03 November 2024) shared on PacNet on 08 November 2024.

From 22 October to 15 November 2024, the Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department, did not detect additional suspected or confirmed typhoid cases. Since 5 June, a total of 112 cases (23 laboratory confirmed and 89 suspected cases) have been diagnosed, with 21 requiring hospitalisations. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Personal exchanges with country focal person on 15 November 2024.

In EpiWeek 2, 69 new dengue cases were reported, including residents of Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Raiatea, Ua Pou, Rangiroa, Tikehau and one visitor. The total number of reported cases is 729 (6283 confirmed cases and 46 probable cases) since November 27, 2023. The incidence and positivity rate are decreasing compared to previous weeks. However, vigilance remains essential during this rainy season and the back-to-school period. In EpiWeek 2, two new hospitalisations were reported in individuals aged 11 and 30 years old. Since the beginning of the epidemic, no severe cases or deaths have been reported. Since late July, DENV-1 has become the predominant serotype in the country, representing 100% of serotyped samples since in EpiWeek 51, 2024. The blue alert for DENV-1 is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°2 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 21 January 2025.

In EpiWeek 2, 18 new influenza cases (14 type A and 4 type B) were reported, out of 97 test results submitted. A significant increase in the positivity rate was observed (19% compared to 4% in EpiWeek 1). Among these cases, four hospitalisations were reported (1 child aged 2 years and 3 individuals over 60 years old). Two of the individuals over 60 years of age had associated comorbidities. None of the four hospitalised individuals were vaccinated. In the international context, these results suggest the beginning of an epidemic, a red alert for Influenza A is added. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°2 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 21 January 2025.

Between 14 June 2024 and 12 January 2025, 578 confirmed pertussis cases were reported. In EpiWeek 2, 29 new cases were recorded including residents of Tahiti, Tahaa and Raiatea. One hospitalisation was reported in EpiWeek 2 for a person over 60 years old. An upward trend in incidence has been observed over the past two weeks. However, compared to the previous week, a 40% increase in the number of tests conducted has led to a decrease in the positivity rate. The red alert is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°2 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 21 January 2025.

As of 17 January 2025, the government of New Caledonia, through the Department of Health and Social Affairs (“Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales, DASS), raised an alert to the population regarding an influenza epidemic in New Caledonia. Currently, there is an active circulation of respiratory viruses, the pressure on hospital services and general medical practices is intensifying. In the current context, faced in New Caledonia a red alert for Influenza is added. – Source: 2025.01.17_cp_epidemie_de_grippe.pdf accessed on 21 January 2025.

As of 20 January 2025, 190 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024, out of 1,227 samples tested, six new cases since the 14 January 2025. Since the 1st of January 2025, 22 new cases have been reported, with the most recent case dated 14 January 2025. The blue alert is maintained. – Sources: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie accessed on 21 January 2025.

In EpiWeek 2 (week ending January 10, 2025), weekly pertussis cases in New Zealand increased to 108 from 72 in EpiWeek 1, bringing the total reported cases in January 2025 to 135. According to the latest report from the Institute of Environmental Science and Research (ESR), 402 pertussis cases (291 confirmed and 111 probable) were reported between December 14, 2024, and January 10, 2025, compared to 568 cases in the preceding four weeks. The decrease in case numbers is partially attributed to reduced case ascertainment during the Christmas holiday period. However, one death was reported during this period. Since the start of the national epidemic, 101 cases (8.2%) have required hospitalisation, with 48 (55.2%) of the 87 cases in infants under 1 year hospitalised. The blue alert is maintained. – Sources: Pertussis dashboard and Pertussis report 14 December 2024–10 January 2025 accessed on 21 January 2025.

As of 12 January 2025, a total of 352 pertussis cases (24 confirmed and 328 suspected) have been reported by Samoa's Ministry of Health between EpiWeeks 46 (2024) and EpiWeek 2 (2025). An additional 31 cases were reported since the 05 January 2025. The calculated cumulative incidence rate increased from 156.2 cases per 100,000 people to 171.2 cases per 100,00 people between September 2024 and 12 January 2025. The majority of cases (50%) occurred in infants under five years old. Since September 2024, 41% of cases were hospitalised. The red alert is maintained. – Source:  Ministry of Health – Pertussis Surveillance Situation Report N°7 (EpiWeek 02: 06 – 12 January 2025) shared on PacNet on 20 January 2025.

In EpiWeek 1 (30 Dec 2024 – 5 Jan 2025), the National Surveillance unit recorded 360 cases of influenza-like illness in Efate Island, surpassing the alert threshold of 268 cases per week prompting the Ministry of Health to declare a seasonal influenza outbreak for the island. The majority of cases originated from Ohlen, Mele, and Bladinere, with no deaths reported. As of 05 January, the causative agent remains unconfirmed due to a lack of lab testing. The Ministry of Health is collaborating with partners to facilitate overseas specimen testing while emphasizing the seasonal nature of such respiratory viruses. Consequently, a grey alert for influenza-like illness is added, awaiting confirmation of the causative agent. – Source: Efate Island Seasonal Influenza Outbreak – Situation Report #1 (report date: 13/01/2025; covering period from 30 December 2024 – 05 January 2025) shared on PacNet on 15 January 2025.

As of 22 January 2025, The Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Public Health Department, did not report any additional confirmed typhoid cases; however, there are still some reports of prolonged fever. Since 5 June 2024, a total of 112 cases (23 laboratory confirmed and 89 suspected cases) have been diagnosed, with 21 requiring hospitalisations. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Personal exchanges with country focal person on 21 January 2025

As of 03 March 2025, Niue’s Department of Health reported five active COVID-19 cases, two from the previous day and three newly confirmed cases. Health authorities urge residents to remain vigilant, test if symptomatic, and minimise contact if positive. Preventive measures are strongly recommended to reduce community transmission. As the Department of Health continues to monitor the situation, the COVID-19 alert level has been downgraded from red to blue. – Source: Personal exchanges with country focal person on 03 March 2025.

As of 16 March 2025, a total of 418 pertussis cases (24 confirmed and 394 suspected) have been reported by Samoa's Ministry of Health between EpiWeek 46 (2024) and EpiWeek 11 (2025). The calculated cumulative incidence rate is 203.4 cases per 100,000 people. Among the 24 confirmed cases, 67% are infants under one year old, with incomplete or no vaccination in most cases, and 39% of all cases required hospitalization at Tupua Tamases Meaole Hospital (TTMH). The blue alert is maintained. – Source:  Ministry of Health – Pertussis Surveillance Situation Report N°16 (EpiWeek 11: 10 – 16 March 2025) shared to PPHSN Focal Point on 21 March 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: As of 23 March 2025, the Health Ministry has reported that there have been over 5,100 cases of dengue fever nationally and a dengue death of a high school student from the Western Division. The Ministry declared a dengue fever outbreak in the Western Division on the 03 February and launched targeted interventions, including house-to-house surveillance, larviciding, mosquito control measures and public awareness programs. The dengue serotypes causing the current outbreak are Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2) and 3 (DENV-3). The red alert for DENV-2 and DENV-3 is maintained. - Source: Ministry of Health and Medical Services,  Ministry Confirms Another Dengue Death and Prevention and Press Release on Dengue Fever and Leptospirosis accessed on 08 April 2025.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: In EpiWeek 13, 60 new cases (55 confirmed and 05 probable) were reported. Since November 27, 2023, a total of 1,517 cases have been recorded, including 1,377 confirmed and 140 probable cases. Two new hospitalisations were reported in EpiWeek 13. Both the positivity and hospitalisation rates decreased compared to EpiWeek 12. The blue alert for DENV-1 is maintained. – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°12 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 April 2025.
source_names: Bulletin de Surveillance en Polynésie française

records.description: In EpiWeek 13, 22 new influenza cases (17 type A, 05 type B) were reported. Among these cases, there were eleven hospitalisations reported. Since EpiWeek 03, 459 influenza cases were reported (94% type A and 6% type B), with a total of 141 hospitalisations and ten deaths. Both positivity and hospitalisation rates have increased during this reporting period. The blue alert for influenza A is maintained.  – Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°13 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 April 2025.

Since June 14, 2024, a total of 691 confirmed cases of pertussis have been reported. Pertussis activity slightly increased in EpiWeek 13, with positivity rates showing an increase trend. A total of 23 hospitalisations have been reported since June 14, 2024, and one death was recorded in EpiWeek 46 of 2024 in an infant. Since the last report, two additional cases have been reported. The blue alert is maintained. Source: Bulletin de surveillance sanitaire de Polynésie française n°12 - 2025 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 08 April 2025.
source_names: Bulletin de Surveillance en Polynésie française

records.description: As of 07 April 2025, 218 cases of pertussis have been reported since April 2024, out of 1,440 samples tested. In 2025, 47 new cases have been reported with 32 cases recorded in January, ten cases in February and five cases reported in this current month. The most recent case was reported on 24 March 2025. The blue alert is maintained. – Source: Coqueluche | Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie accessed on 08 April 2025.

As of week ending on 28th March, weekly pertussis cases in New Zealand increased to 51 from 42 in week ending on 21 March, bringing the total reported cases since the beginning of 2025 to 1044. According to the latest report from the Institute of Environmental Science and Research (ESR), since the start of the national epidemic on 19 October 2024, 2,075 confirmed, probable and suspect cases have been notified. Of these, 175 cases (9.0%) have required hospitalisation with one reported death, with 84 (53.2%) of the 160 cases in infants under 1 year hospitalised. The blue alert is maintained. – Sources: Pertussis dashboard and Pertussis report 22 February–21 March 2025 accessed on 08 April 2025.

As of 07 April 2025, the Ministry of Health reported ten new dengue cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total confirmed cases to 445 since the declaration of the Outbreak on 19 February 2025, primarily affecting 10-19-year-olds. Ten patients are currently hospitalised, all reported to be in stable condition, with no death reported so far. Authorities continue case investigations, mosquito control and public awareness efforts, urging residents to eliminate breeding sites, use protective measures, and seek medical attention for severe symptoms. The serotype that is responsible for this current outbreak is Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2) identified by the Victorian Infectious Diseases Reference Laboratory (VIDRL), Melbourne Australia. The red alert for DENV-2 is maintained. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak, Situation report #40 (07 April 2025) shared on PacNet on 07 April 2025.

As of 23 March 2025, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services reported 5,128 cases of dengue nationally with 2841 cases in the Western division, 1095 cases in the North, 1090 cases in Central and 102 cases in the Eastern division. Additionally, there has been 1,511 admissions nationwide with 4 deaths reported. In addition to the ongoing outbreak that was declared in the Western division on 03 February 2025, the Ministry of Health and Medical Services have since declared a dengue fever outbreak in the Central Division on 11 April 2025  with the most recent increase of cases in March seen to be above the expected levels for the same period last year. The surge in cases have been observed over the last three weeks in the subdivisions within Central while there has also been an increase in admissions of dengue fever cases at the subdivisional hospitals and at the main tertiary hospital. Targeted interventions continue, including house-to-house surveillance, larviciding, mosquito control measures and public awareness programs. The dengue serotypes causing the current outbreak are Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2) and 3 (DENV-3). The red alert for DENV-2 and DENV-3 is maintained. - Source: Ministry of Health and Medical Services, Press release on Dengue Fever and Leptospirosis and Press Release on Dengue Fever Oubreak for the Central Division accessed on 15 April 2025.
source_names: Fiji Ministry of Health & Medical Services Website

records.description: On the 26 March 2025, the Niue Health Department declared an outbreak of Influenza A in Niue following an increase in symptomatic cases across multiple age groups and villages. As of 1st May 2025, there have been 88 confirmed cases, nineteen hospitalisations with the highest number of individuals affected in the 11-18 years and 50-64 years age groups. The Health Department is currently managing the outbreak and advises minimizing social gatherings, wearing masks, practicing good hygiene, staying home if unwell and seeking medical attention for severe symptoms. The red alert for influenza A is maintained.  – Source: Niue Influenza A Outbreak Situation Report #4 – 2025 shared on Niue Public Health Division  accessed on 13 May 2025.

Papua New Guinea: As of 14 May 2025, the Papua New Guinea government activated its National Polio Preparedness and Immunisation Response Plan. This is in response to the detection of the vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2) in environmental samples in Port Moresby and in two children in Lae Morobe Province, confirming the presence of the virus in the community. The World Health Organization has declared a polio outbreak in Papua New Guinea following the detection of the viruses. Vaccination efforts are being intensified, with two nationwide vaccination campaigns planned, expanded disease monitoring, and support from WHO, UNICEF, and the Australian government to prevent further spread. The outbreak poses a significant risk to young children, especially in areas with low vaccination rates, and concerns are being raised about potential spread to neighbouring countries. As a result, a red alert for Polio is added. - Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health and Polio outbreak confirmed in Papua New Guinea, World Health Organization says accessed on 20 May 2025.

Cook Islands: The Ministry of Health has officially declared a dengue fever outbreak in Rarotonga on 22 May 2025, following confirmation of two new cases since 19 May. As of 22 May 2025, a total of 7 locally acquired dengue cases have been reported in the past 18 days reaching the outbreak threshold. Since February 2025, a total of eleven isolated cases have been recorded, with Tupapa recording the highest number of dengue cases, five out of eleven cases. Local transmission has been confirmed. The serotypes that are responsible for this current outbreak are Dengue Virus Type 1 (DENV-1) and Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2). Stakeholder meetings are underway, and an island-wide clean-up and peri-focal spraying will continue for two weeks. Surveillance has expanded to the Pa Enua, and clinics remain on high alert. WHO and regional partners have been notified. No travel restrictions are in place, but precautions are advised. The public is urged to eliminate mosquito breeding sites, use repellents, wear long sleeves, and seek medical care if symptoms appear. A red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 is added. – Sources: Dengue Fever Outbreak Media Release, Operation Namu activated as dengue cases rise in Rarotonga and Tupapa hit hardest by dengue outbreak accessed on 27 May 2025.

French Polynesia: In EpiWeek 20, 48 new dengue cases (41 confirmed and 7 probable) were reported. Since November 27, 2023, a total of 2,024 cases have been recorded, including 1,816 confirmed and 208 probable cases. Four new hospitalisation was reported in EpiWeek 20. The positivity and hospitalisation rate increased compared to EpiWeek 19. Solomon Islands: Since 8 June 2025, the Solomon Islands Ministry of Health and Medical Services has been actively monitoring the outbreak of diarrheal illness in Honiara and Guadalcanal. As of 6 July 2025, 3226 diarrhea cases were reported from six provinces, Honiara, Guadalcanal, Central, Choiseul, Isabel and Temotu which included one death in a 2-year-old child who had a history of diarrhea and vomiting. Most of the cases reported are in the age group 1-4 years with 78% of the total cases below 5years. As of 11 July 2025, 12 out of 23 stool samples collected were positive for rotavirus. The Ministry of Health and Medical Services is urging the public to maintain strict hygiene practices and ensure children are vaccinated, as the virus is highly contagious and can be deadly for young children. Health authorities are actively monitoring the situation, coordinating with hospitals and the WHO, and advising immediate medical attention for any symptoms of diarrhea or vomiting. records.description: Wallis and Futuna: On 22 July 2025, the Wallis and Futuna Health Agency declared an outbreak of influenza along with active circulation of SARS-CoV-2, following the rise in reported cases since the beginning of July. As of 24 August 2025, a 40% increase in influenza-like illness was observed in Futuna compared to the previous week, along with three confirmed cases of influenza A in Wallis. Wallis also saw a 20% rise in paracetamol prescriptions. The Health Agency urges the public to follow key prevention measures such as mask-wearing, handwashing, and avoiding contact with vulnerable individuals. The public are advised to seek medical attention when symptoms appear or contact emergency services if experiencing severe respiratory issues. The red alert for Influenza is maintained– Source: Alerte - Epidemie de virus respiratoires - Wallis et Futuna and Personal exchange with country focal point on 27 August 2025.

Papua New Guinea: The national poliovirus outbreak was declared on 15 May 2025, following detections in Lae and Port Moresby, with genetic testing confirming that the vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2) strain originated from Indonesia. As of 28 August 2025, the National Department of Health (NDoH), in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) and partners, confirmed the first human case of paralytic poliomyelitis (cVDPV2) in Papua New Guinea. The case involves a 4-year-old unvaccinated male from Lae, Morobe Province, who developed acute flaccid paralysis, with onset of paralysis on 9 July. This confirms that the virus has transitioned from environmental detection to direct impact on children. Since May 2025, over 31 cases of cVDPV2 have been detected through environmental and community surveillance. Papua New Guinea have launched a Supplementary Immunization Activity (SIA) on 11 August 2025, targeting children under 10 years with the novel oral polio vaccine (nOPV2). As of 26 August, national coverage stands at 41.2%, with Hela Province leading at 91%. The campaign includes two vaccination rounds and emphasizes both oral and injectable vaccines, with strong involvement from schools, parents, and community leaders to ensure wide coverage. The second round of SIA is scheduled from 29 September to 17 October.  The red alert is maintained. – Sources: Country updates as of 03 September 2025 and Papua New Guinea Launches National Polio Immunization Campaign to Protect Every Child accessed on 9 September 2025.

The red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 is maintained. – Source: DOH Update accessed on 23 September 2025.

Australia:  Queensland Health has reported an ongoing measles outbreak in Cairns, with 12 confirmed cases identified since 1 September 2025. Active measles alerts are currently in place for Cairns, Gold Coast, Mackay and Townsville. As of 19 September, New South Wales (NSW) Health confirmed a measles case who was infectious while visiting several locations in Northern NSW and Sydney, including flights from Perth to Sydney and Sydney to Gold Coast. Additionally, a separate confirmed case has been linked to recent travel from Indonesia. Western Australia (WA) has also issued a measles alert, with new public exposure sites identified across Queensland, NSW and WA. Individuals who visited the listed exposure sites during the specified dates and times are advised to monitor for symptoms for up to three weeks from the exposure date, seek medical advice if symptoms develop and to check their vaccination status is up to date. A red alert for measles in Queensland is added– Sources: Measles alert for Cairns, Measles alert for Sydney’s north western suburbs, Measles alert for Sydney Airport and Northern NSW and Measles alert accessed on 23 September 2025.

Children under 15 years account for 73% of cases, and the circulating serotypes remain predominantly DENV-1 (91%) and DENV-2 (9%). Case numbers decreased by 25% (218) compared to the previous EpiWeek, with 650 new clinical cases of which 164 are lab confirmed. Hospital admissions decreased by 38%, with 73 new admissions, 84 discharges, and 21 patients still hospitalised, none in ICU. The Ministry of Health continues its whole-of-government response through the Integrated Vector Control Committee, focusing on source reduction, environmental sanitation, and widespread risk communication. As a result, the red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 is changed to blue. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report in Samoa Issue No.22 accessed on 23 September 2025.

The most affected districts were Anoamaa 1 (56 cases) in Upolu and Palauli 2 (13 cases) district in Savai’i. The Ministry of Health continues its whole-of-government response through the Integrated Vector Control Committee, focusing on source reduction, environmental sanitation, and widespread risk communication. Since 24 August 2025, there has been a sustained decrease in reported clinically diagnosed cases, and since 31 August 2025, a decline in laboratory-confirmed cases. As a result, the red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 is changed to blue. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report in Samoa Issue No.22 accessed on 23 September 2025.

Tuvalu: The Tuvalu Department of Health declared a dengue outbreak on 5 June 2025. As of 21 September 2025, 620 suspected cases were tested, with 193 confirmed positive. The dengue cases are widely distributed along Fongafale and two outer islands, Nanumaga (5 cases) and Nukufetau (6 cases). The outbreak is due to Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2). Currently, 8% of cases have recovered, while 21 remain active. 12 patients (six children and six adults) have been hospitalised since the start of the outbreak, with no current admissions and no deaths reported. Children under 14 years account for over two-thirds of cases ranging in age from 3 months to 62 years. Of the confirmed cases, 115 cases are males and 78 females. Hotspots include Fakaifou, Senala, Alapi and Lofeagai. In EpiWeek 38 (15-21 September), 17 new cases were detected, with 21% positivity rate, showing a decrease compared to the previous week. The Department of Health continues to implement control measures, including response team coordination, case investigations and vector control,  staff training by PacMOSSI, targeted spraying and ongoing public awareness through talkback shows and community engagement. The red alert for DENV-2 is maintained. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak, Situation report #12 (21 September 2025) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 23 September 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: New Zealand: As of the week ending on 12 September, weekly pertussis cases in New Zealand increased to 49 from 34 in the week ending on 5 September, bringing the total reported cases since the beginning of 2025 to 1,973. According to the latest report from the New Zealand Institute for Public Health and Forensic Science (PHF Science), 2,933 confirmed, probable and suspect cases have been notified since the start of the national epidemic on 19 October 2024. Of these, 259 cases (9.2%) have required hospitalisation with one reported death. 122 (50.4%) out of the 245 cases in infants under 1 year have been hospitalised. The blue alert is maintained. – Sources: Pertussis dashboard and Pertussis Report 26 July–22 August 2025 accessed on 23 September 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Nauru: Dengue cases were first reported by the Republic of Nauru (RON) Hospital on 27 June 2025. As of 21 September 2025, the Ministry of Health has not reported any new cases since the last PacNet update on 23 September, thus confirmed case numbers remain at 453 out of the 1,542 tests conducted. Two fatalities were recorded on 30 July 2025, a 15-year-old male and 17-year-old female, with no current hospital admissions. The majority of cases are among children in the age of 5-10 years with 76% of the total cases being less than 18 years old. The cases are widely distributed across the island, with most of the cases from Aiwo, Denigomodu, Meneng, Buada, Anetan, Boe and Baitsi. Vector control activities, including thermal fogging, residual spraying and peri-focal spraying are being conducted in the households of confirmed cases. The public is advised to eliminate mosquito breeding sites, protect themselves from mosquito bites and seek prompt medical attention if symptoms appear. The blue alert for DENV-2 is maintained. – Sources: Nauru Bulletin Issue 11 and Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report #72 (21 September) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 30 September 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Papua New Guinea: The national poliovirus outbreak was declared on 15 May 2025, following detections in Lae and Port Moresby, with genetic testing confirming that the vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2) strain originated from Indonesia. As of 28 August 2025, the National Department of Health (NDoH), in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) and partners, confirmed the first human case of paralytic poliomyelitis (cVDPV2) in Papua New Guinea. Since then, as of 31 October 2025 an additional 4 human polio virus cases have been reported, with 59 cases of cVDPV2 have been detected through environmental and community surveillance across multiple provinces indicating ongoing virus circulation. Papua New Guinea have launched a Supplementary Immunization Activity (SIA) on 11 August 2025, targeting children under 10 years with the novel oral polio vaccine (nOPV2). Despite launching two rounds of national immunization campaigns, coverage remains below the 95% target, with national averages around 47% for both nOPV2 and fractional-dose inactivated polio vaccine (fIPV). Surveillance efforts are active but face challenges, including low stool adequacy rates and routine immunization coverage below 60% in key provinces like Morobe, Enga, and Central. The red alert remains in effect. – Sources: Country updates as of 03 September 2025, Papua New Guinea Launches National Polio Immunization Campaign to Protect Every Child and Polio Outbreak PNG Situation Report No. 16 (31 October 2025) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 18 November 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Kiribati: The Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) confirmed a dengue outbreak on 24 April 2025, after a significant rise in confirmed cases. As of 11 December 2025, MHMS reported a total of 503 confirmed dengue cases and 1,510 suspected dengue cases with 68 hospitalisations, all of which have been discharged, and one confirmed death. There have been 5 new cases since the last report on 19 November 2025. Dengue cases range in age from 1 month to 95 years, with the most affected group being those aged 3 to 9 years. Among all reported cases, 55% are female and 45% male. The serotypes that are responsible for this current outbreak are Dengue Virus Type 1 (DENV-1) and Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2), tested at VIDRL in Melbourne. The MHMS continues to promote health awareness on social media through posters, press releases, and videos. It continues to investigate cases, conduct house-to-house inspections in high-risk areas, eliminate mosquito breeding sites, and advise community members to maintain a clean and healthy environment. Based on the sustained decline in case numbers for the past four weeks, the blue alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Fever Situational Report #30 (11 December 2025) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 11 December 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Tuvalu: The Tuvalu Department of Health declared a dengue outbreak on 5 June 2025. As of 12 December 2025, 938 suspected cases were tested, with 1 new case reported since the last update on 9 December 2025. The total number of confirmed positive cases is 249. The dengue cases are widely distributed along Fongafale, one atoll, Amatuku and three outer islands, Nanumaga (9 cases) Nukufetau (14 cases) and Vaitupu (1 case). The outbreak is due to Dengue Virus Type 2 (DENV-2). Currently, 99% of cases have recovered, while 1 remain active. 12 patients (six children and six adults) have been hospitalised since the start of the outbreak, with no current admissions and no deaths reported. Children under 14 years account for 73% of cases ranging in age from 3 months to 80 years. Of the confirmed cases, 149 cases are males and 100 females. The Department of Health continues to conduct case investigations along with physical vector control on Funafuti. The blue alert for DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak, Situation report #24 (12 December 2025) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 16 December 2025.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: American Samoa: On 8 July 2025, American Samoa declared a public health emergency in response to a dengue outbreak. As of 4 January 2026, 16 new cases have been reported, bringing the total to 566 lab-confirmed cases. Of these cases, 288 individuals required hospitalisation at some point during their illness with no severe complications or dengue haemorrhagic fever observed. Of the five hundred sixty-six confirmed cases, four hundred twenty-three are children and one hundred forty-three are adults. Molecular sequencing conducted by the laboratory confirmed co-circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2 with sixty-six cases identified as DENV-1 and four cases as DENV-2. The public health response actions involve a multi-sector response, targeted spraying at residences of local confirmed cases up to 250 metres, fogging of high-risk areas, weekly public awareness campaigns and urging the public to take preventive measures such as avoiding mosquito bites, eliminating mosquito breeding sites, and supporting community-based vector control efforts. The red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: American Samoa Department of Health Dengue Response Sitrep 26, 5 January 2026 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 11 January 2026.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Vanuatu: The Vanuatu Ministry of Health continues to monitor the pertussis outbreak, with two new cases reported in EpiWeek 04, bringing the cumulative total to 760 cases since the outbreak was declared on 18 August 2025, including 732 clinically diagnosed and 28 laboratory‑confirmed cases. No deaths or hospitalisations were recorded this week, and overall pertussis activity is steadily declining, with weekly case numbers having dropped notably since EW01. However, transmission remains above the alert threshold, indicating ongoing spread. The most affected age groups continue to be children aged 2–5 years and individuals over 5 years, while infants under three months represent only a small proportion of total cases. To date, the outbreak has resulted in three infant deaths. Geographically, the majority of cases have been reported from Efate (54%) followed by Tanna (37%). The red alert for pertussis is changed to blue.  – Sources: Vanuatu Pertussis Outbreak: Situation Report 11 (26 January 2026) shared on PacNet on 27 January 2026.

In Futuna, influenza-like illness (ILI) activity during EpiWeek 04 (19–25 January 2026) remains elevated, with syndromic and non-specific indicators close to or slightly above established thresholds. However, overall trends appear stable with no sharp increase observed, and influenza A detections continue at a low level (2 cases). In Wallis, consultations and urgent care visits stay below seasonal thresholds, syndromic indicators show no major surge, and no influenza A detections were reported. Overall, both islands show no strong epidemic growth, with Futuna maintaining modest but persistent ILI circulation and Wallis remaining largely within seasonal norms. The blue alert for Influenza A remains in effect. – Source: Tableau de bord de la surveillance multi source - ADSWF accessed on 03 February 2027.

Measles activity in Australia continues to rise across multiple states and territories, with Victoria now reporting six confirmed cases in 2026, all linked to overseas travel, and new public exposure sites prompting strengthened vaccination and surveillance messaging. In New South Wales, two additional cases were confirmed in Sydney: one locally acquired and one imported bringing the state’s total to 10 cases since 1 January 2026, with multiple exposure sites identified across Sydney. South Australia has confirmed its third case of 2026, an infant infected overseas, with several exposure sites listed though no ongoing risk remains, while Queensland reports eight cases to date, evenly split between imported infections and local transmission linked to those imported cases. The Northern Territory has not confirmed any measles cases in 2026 but remains on high alert due to significant interstate and international measles activity, emphasising vaccination checks and strict clinical protocols given Australia’s continued importation driven transmission risk. The red alert for measles in Australia remains in effect. – Sources: Chief Health Officer Alert - New measles cases in Victoria - 6 February 2026, Measles alert for Sydney, Measles case 5 February 2026 | SA Health, Notifiable conditions reports: Summary information | Queensland Health, CDC surveillance update - January 2026 and National Communicable Diseases Surveillance Dashboard accessed on 10 February 2026.

The Cook Islands dengue outbreak continues to escalate, with 614 probables, confirmed, and suspected cases to date, including 75 active cases, 513 recoveries, and 40 total hospitalisations. The first dengue related death was reported on 2 February 2026, an elderly person with underlying medical conditions. In response to rising transmission on Rarotonga and detected cases in Aitutaki, Atiu, Mauke and Mangaia, Te Marae Ora has launched Operation Namu26, a national 30–60 day intensified intervention involving coordinated vector control, island wide clean ups, strengthened community mobilisation, expanded perifocal and block spraying, and enhanced surveillance across the Pa Enua. Tourism operators, Red Cross teams, island governments, and Puna communities are actively supporting prevention efforts through spraying, risk communication, and distribution of dengue prevention packs. The blue alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Situational Report - Te Marae Ora Cook Islands Ministry of Health and Operation Namu26 launched to strengthen national dengue response - Te Marae Ora Cook Islands Ministry of Health accessed on 10 February 2026.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Influenza like illness (ILI) activity in the Marshall Islands remains elevated in EpiWeek 05, with 28 ILI cases in Majuro, 2 in Ebeye, and 37 cases reported across outer island health centers, several of which exceeded their population based alert thresholds, indicating persistent localized transmission. Although national trends show a continuation of the gradual decline observed in earlier weeks, outer island communities continue to report clusters above alert levels, reflecting uneven transmission dynamics.  The aetiology is yet to be determined thus a grey alert for ILI remains in effect. – Source: RMI Communicable Disease Weekly Report for EpiWeek 05 (26 January – 01 February 2026) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 05 February2026.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: As of the week ending on 30 January 2026, weekly pertussis cases in New Zealand decreased to 53 cases as compared to 58 in previous week ending on 23 January, bringing the total reported cases since the beginning of 2026 to 243. The blue alert for pertussis remains in effect. – Sources: Pertussis dashboard accessed on 10 February 2026.

Samoa continues to experience a prolonged dengue outbreak, with 16,482 cumulative cases reported from 1 January 2025 to 1 February 2026. During EpiWeek 05 (26 January – 01 February 2026), 56 new cases were recorded, including 11 new hospital admissions, marking increases compared to the previous week, while 35 cases were laboratory confirmed and no ICU admissions were reported. Although case numbers had decreased earlier in January, recent weeks show rising presentations with dengue like symptoms, with higher concentrations of cases in North West Upolu (Vaimauga–Sagaga) and Savaii (Faasaleleaga and Palauli), reflecting sustained community transmission across both main islands. One additional death was reported in EpiWeek 05, a seven month old infant bringing the total deaths to eight. Public health authorities continue to urge environmental clean ups, mosquito bite prevention, and early care seeking. The blue alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report in Samoa (issue No.42, EpiWeek 05) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 04 February 2026 & CURRENT COMMUNICABLE DISEASE STATUS AND PUBLIC HEALTH ADVISORY accessed on 03 February 2026.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: As of 12 February 2026, dengue transmission remains ongoing in American Samoa, with a total of 782 laboratory‑confirmed cases reported since the outbreak was declared in July 2025. The majority of cases are paediatric, particularly among children aged 11–15 years. Overall transmission activity remains high and is expected to increase in the coming weeks, although most cases have been managed without complications, largely due to early medical presentation. The Department of Health continues to implement control measures, including targeted mosquito spraying, larval source reduction, and village‑level outreach, alongside sustained public messaging urging residents to take preventive actions to reduce mosquito exposure and eliminate breeding sites. The red alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: DoH records 782 confirmed cases of dengue fever | Talanei accessed on 17 February

As of 30 January 2026, dengue activity in Tuvalu has declined, with no new dengue cases reported since EpiWeek 04. Since the outbreak was declared on 5 June 2025, a total of 998 dengue‑like illness cases have been tested, of which 256 were RDT‑positive, all associated with DENV‑2. All reported cases have fully recovered, and no deaths have been recorded. Transmission was previously widespread across Funafuti, Amatuku, Funafala, and the outer islands of Nanumaga, Nukufetau, and Vaitupu, with children under 14 years accounting for more than two‑thirds of cases. The Department of Health continues surveillance, case investigations, and community‑level vector control activities to prevent resurgence and ensure early detection. The blue alert for DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Fever Outbreak, Situation report #31 (24th- 30th January 2026) shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body focal point on 12 February 2026.
source_names: Country Reports share to PPHSN Focal Point

records.description: Dengue transmission continues in Kiribati, with the outbreak ongoing since April 2025. As of 13 April 2026, a cumulative total of 514 laboratory confirmed cases and 1,564 suspected cases have been reported nationwide. During the most recent reporting period, two new confirmed cases and 27 new suspected cases were notified. Transmission remains concentrated in South Tarawa, which accounts for the majority of reported cases. Both DENV 1 and DENV 2 continue to circulate, with most cases described as mild, although one death and 68 hospitalisations have been reported to date. The blue alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Dengue Fever Situational Report 32 shared with PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 10 April 2026.

records.description: As of 24 April 2026, dengue activity in the Cook Islands has remained low, with only isolated cases reported and no evidence of sustained transmission. Between 6 and 22 April 2026, single cases were reported on 9, 13, 14 and 20 April, all on Rarotonga, while no cases have been reported from Aitutaki or Atiu during the past month and none from Mauke and Mangaia for several months. Given the sustained reduction in reported cases, Operation Namu26 has concluded, and routine public health surveillance and monitoring are continuing as authorities work towards a possible declaration of dengue free status. The blue alert for DENV-1 and DENV-2 remains in effect. – Source: Operation Namu26 Weekly Update 10 - Te Marae Ora Cook Islands Ministry of Health accessed on 28 April 2026.
